topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the class and outlines how the lecture will cover the initiation and resolution of immune inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition of infection and damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system senses pathogens and cellular stress through molecular danger patterns, pattern recognition receptor families, and downstream signaling cascades.

topics.label: Leukocyte recruitment, cell trafficking, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell migration into tissues and lymph nodes, as well as the severe systemic risks that arise when inflammatory signaling becomes excessive.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, wound healing, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammatory responses, coordinate tissue repair, and lead to chronic inflammatory states or granuloma formation when resolution fails.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and announces the upcoming topic on complement.
